# Data flow

How the ND-100, ND-110 and ND-120 execute an instruction: where the ALU gets its operands, what the destinations do, the sources of the internal data bus and the effects of the commands.

Source: [`defs/runtime/data-flow.yaml`](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/nd-microcode-meta/blob/main/defs/runtime/data-flow.yaml).

## Header of `data-flow.yaml`

```text
ND-100/110/120 Microcode Runtime Data Flow

Runtime semantics derived from the ND-110 CPU emulator source
(the ND110CPU C# project). Specifically:
  BUFALU.cs  (SetRS, ExecuteALUOperation, ExecuteAluDestination)
  Cpu.cs     (Execute_1_LatchInternalBus, Execute_2_LatchALU,
              Execute_3_Commands, Execute_4_ConditionControl)

The ND-110 ALU is built around Am2901 4-bit bit-slices. The operand
routing below reflects the Am2901 model with the ND-specific
extensions (RASEL/RBSEL, STS, paging, etc.).
```

## Model family

nd100, nd110, nd120

## Operand roles

| Key | token\_pattern | field | bits | role | write\_access | override\_by | dual\_use\_note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `a_operand` | A,&lt;name&gt; | AOP | 15, 12 | Selects which register feeds ALU operand R when ALUSrc uses A | no | RASEL |  |
| `b_operand` | B,&lt;name&gt; | BOP | 19, 16 | Selects which register feeds ALU operand S when ALUSrc uses B, AND the destination register when ALUD,B is specified | yes | RBSEL | B is BOTH an ALU input (read) AND the output destination (write)<br>when ALUD,B is used. Example:<br>B,T ALUF,PASSD ALUD,B IDBS,ARG ... 13;<br>Writes 0o13 to the T register via:<br>IDB=13 -&gt; ALU.D=13 -&gt; F=D -&gt; F-&gt;B -&gt; T register |

## ALU sources

| Key | name | R | S | am2901 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | A\_Q | A register | Q (internal) | AQ |
| `1` | A\_B | A register | B register | AB |
| `2` | O\_Q | 0 (constant) | Q (internal) | ZQ |
| `3` | O\_B | 0 (constant) | B register | ZB |
| `4` | O\_A | 0 (constant) | A register | ZA |
| `5` | D\_A | D (IDB latched) | A register | DA |
| `6` | D\_Q | D (IDB latched) | Q (internal) | DQ |
| `7` | D\_O | D (IDB latched) | 0 (constant) | DZ |

## ALUD behavior

| Key | name | y\_bus | q\_update | b\_register\_write | shift | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | QREG | F | Q := F |  | none |  |
| `1` | NOP | F |  |  | none | ALU result travels on the Y bus (consumed by IDB source 0) but is not stored. |
| `2` | RAMA | Reg\[AOP\] |  | Reg\[BOP\] := F | none |  |
| `3` | RAMF | F |  | Reg\[BOP\] := F | none | Standard result write. The B register selected by B,&lt;name&gt; gets F.<br>This is the most common ALU destination. |
| `4` | RAMQD | F | Q := Q &gt;&gt; 1 (Q\[15\] &lt;- QLI) | Reg\[BOP\] := F &gt;&gt; 1 (F\[15\] &lt;- RRI) | right\_double | Double right-shift for multiply/divide sequences. |
| `5` | RAMD | F |  | Reg\[BOP\] := F &gt;&gt; 1 (F\[15\] &lt;- RRI) | right\_single |  |
| `6` | RAMQU | F | Q := Q &lt;&lt; 1 (Q\[0\] &lt;- QLI) | Reg\[BOP\] := F &lt;&lt; 1 (F\[0\] &lt;- RLI) | left\_double |  |
| `7` | RAMU | F |  | Reg\[BOP\] := F &lt;&lt; 1 (F\[0\] &lt;- RLI) | left\_single |  |

## ND100 branch address selector

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `applies_to` | nd100 |
| `mapj0_bit` | 27 |
| `slwcs0_bit` | 26 |
| `vect0_bit` | 25 |
| `mis_bits` | 43, 42 |
| `notes` | The "L H H" entry has two possible outcomes depending on the<br>asynchronous /INT\_RQ input at the end of the current microcycle.<br>A disassembler should label this mode as "MAPPED" and annotate<br>"runtime picks map-PROM or VECT-IRQ" rather than committing to one. |

### Truth table

| mapj0 | slwcs0 | vect0 | mis | source | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H | H | H | \* | PROM(0..11) | Direct jump to the PROM-supplied 12-bit branch target. |
| H | H | L | 0 | PROM(4..11) \|\| IR(0..3) | Upper 8 bits from PROM, lower 4 from macro-IR bits 0..3. |
| H | H | L | 1 | PROM(4..11) \|\| IR(8..10) | Upper 8 bits from PROM, lower from macro-IR bits 8..10 (zero-extended to 4 bits). |
| H | H | L | 2 | PROM(4..11) \|\| ALD(0..3) | Upper 8 bits from PROM, lower 4 from the auto-load descriptor. |
| H | H | L | 3 | PROM(4..11) \|\| RA(0..3) | Upper 8 bits from PROM, lower 4 from the RA register. |
| L | H | H | \* | map-PROM(IR) if /INT\_RQ | Macro-opcode dispatch via the decode-PLA when no interrupt pending. |
| L | H | H | \* | VECT-IRQ if INT\_RQ | Interrupt vector entry when /INT\_RQ is asserted. |
| L | H | L | \* | ILLEGAL | Reserved / illegal combination. |
| \* | L | \* | \* | START LOAD WRITABLE CS | Initiate writable-control-store load; branch target field is consumed by the WCS load logic instead of the sequencer. |

| `0` | ASH | ASH | Arithmetic shift (sign-preserving). |

### ND100 delta

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | confirmed |
| `reference` | ND-06.018.01 p.25-26 lines 720-748 |
| `summary` | The ND-100 TSEL table has been fully documented from the<br>manual. Deltas vs ND-110:<br>\* Value 0000 differs in semantics (ND-100: "DR=2" tests<br>whether the ALU destination register is P; ND-110:<br>"DR-&gt;Z" - different test).<br>\* Value 1000 is dual-meaning on ND-100 (R=P OR ZF) but<br>single-meaning on ND-110 (R-&gt;P only); ND-110 has ZF<br>separately at 1110.<br>\* Value 1111 differs (ND-100: STP - tests STOP flip-flop;<br>ND-110: SKP - unconditional false / skip).<br>\* Values 0010, 0011, 0101, 0110, 1001 have spelling<br>differences only (INTRQ vs IRQ, RESTRT vs RESTR,<br>DOD vs OOD, DZO vs DZD, OPCTTI vs OPCTT1) - treat as<br>aliases for the same condition. |

### ND100 values

| Key | test | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | DR=2 | Destination register is P. Used to discard prefetch when P is the destination in ROP/BOP instructions. |
| `1` | LCZ | Loop counter is zero. Used to exit fixed-iteration loops. |
| `2` | IRQ | Interrupt request flip-flop. If preceded by CLIRQ, only AM2914 interrupts tested (not PANEL). |
| `3` | RESTR | Current program running in restricted mode. Privileged WCS instructions must test this. |
| `4` | FETCH | Last memory access was a fetch. Used to compute correct P on page fault. |
| `5` | OOD | One-Out-Detect flip-flop (sets TG correctly in FAD/FSB/FMU). Known alias of ND-110 'DOD'. |
| `6` | DZD | Double-Zero-Detect flip-flop (sets TG correctly in FDV). Known alias of ND-110 'DZO'. |
| `7` | COND | Latched true/false result of the previous microinstruction. Postpones the test decision. |
| `8` | R=P OR ZF | DUAL-ROLE on ND-100: detects if a store (STA \*+1) affected the prefetched next location AND serves as the ALU Zero-Flag. ND-110 splits these into separate codes. |
| `9` | OPCTT1 | MOPC terminal test for devices 0o300..0o307 (strap-dependent). If the CPU strap is removed, this line is always false. |
| `10` | OVF | ALU overflow flag. |
| `11` | CRY | ALU carry-out. |
| `12` | F11 | ALU result bit 11. |
| `13` | F15 | ALU result bit 15 (sign bit). |
| `14` | ZF | ALU result is zero. (Also aliased inside TSEL=1000 on ND-100; available standalone here.) |
| `15` | STP | STOP flip-flop is set. Replaces ND-110's SKP at this position. |

## COMM table

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `applies_to` | nd110, nd120 |
| `bits` | 36, 32 |
| `width` | 5 |
| `description` | Microinstruction command field - selects a CPU command or memory op.<br><br>This table holds the BASE mnemonic per code, as taken from the<br>ND-110 hardware-guide OCR. The ND-110 tokens YAML contains<br>compound tokens that bundle a COMM code with additional field<br>values (TC/STS/MIS/sub-selectors) - those variants are listed<br>under \`token\_variants\` for each entry where applicable.<br><br>Note on OCR reconciliation: the OCR source numbered its rows<br>starting from "0 0 0 0 0", but bit-exact validation against<br>ND-110 RASK.CODE (4865/4865 instructions reproduce byte-for-byte)<br>proves that LDIPL / LDPIL is at code 0b00001, not 0b00000. So<br>this table applies a +1 shift relative to the OCR row numbering.<br>COMM=0b00000 means "no command" (default). |
| `reconciliation_summary` | OCR's head (0b00000..0b01110) is off-by-one from the actual hardware encoding - its first row 'LDIPL' is at code 0b00001., OCR scan artefacts detected at codes 0b00010 (LDIPR vs LDGPR), 0b00100 (CLRQ vs CLIRQ), 0b01110 (CLTF vs CLFF). Validated token names win., OCR does not cover codes 0b10011..0b10111, 0b11010, 0b11011 (CJMP/CNEXT/JMP/AWRITE families); these exist in the ND-110 tokens YAML., OCR mnemonics at codes 0b11000/0b11100/0b11101 (EXAMINE/FETCH/DEPOSIT) are the memory-op family names - they group compound tokens AREAD,\*/RDRQ,\*/WRRQ,\* with MIS page-mode sub-selection., Validation authority: nd110-tokens.yaml (bit-exact-verified against RASK.CODE, 4865/4865 instructions). |

#### Name differences

| Key | nd100 | nd110 | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `13` | CLRTI | CLRTC | Both mean 'Clear Real-Time clock Interrupt'; accept either. |

#### Function conflicts

| Key | nd100 | nd110 | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `25` | DERQ | AREAD,XB family | The ND-100 manual explicitly defines 0b11001 = DERQ<br>(Deposit-Request, single variant). The ND-110 tokens<br>YAML uses this code for AREAD,XB / AREAD,XI / IREAD2 /<br>AREAD,NEXT. These are potentially different functions.<br>This is a genuine ND-100/ND-110 function divergence that<br>needs confirmation from the ND-110 hardware guide. |

#### Name aliases

| Key | nd100 | nd110 | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `17` | LDIR (XMM) | LDIR | ND-100 symbolic allows XMM as a synonym for LDIR. |

## Pipeline

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `execute_1` | Decode A/B operands (with RASEL/RBSEL overrides); latch IDB from its selected source |
| `execute_2` | Set ALU modes; compute shift bit inputs; execute ALU; latch Y back to IDB |
| `execute_3` | Execute COMM (commands consume IDB, A-operand, B-operand) |
| `execute_4` | Condition testing (SCOND/ECOND); loop counter update; MIC sequencer picks next address |
